meta.product: Fleet Feet running shoes + fit services
meta.company: Fleet Feet (running specialty retailer, Austin TX location)
meta.thesis: Fleet Feet does not need more shoe SKUs - it needs Austin's new runners to discover the fit-first difference, and Run Your City turns a store visit into a community membership.
meta.variant_angle: local running-store community campaign + shoe prop

business_problem: Fleet Feet sells expert fitting in a city where runners increasingly buy online: 90% of first-time runners quit within a year, often from wrong-shoe injuries, and the store's best asset - free gait analysis and community runs - is invisible to people who have never walked in [R1][R3][S1][S3].

objectives.text: Drive 150 attributed store purchases (event QR + mention code RUNCITY) in 45 days at ~$140 AOV
Capture 600 email/SMS signups via group runs, fit clinics, and the Run Your City challenge
Reach 700K Austin impressions and shift 'shoe store' to 'my running community' - +15 pts among surveyed runners

segments.name: New + Returning Runners (18-40)
segments.demographic: 18-40, students + young professionals, new to running or returning
segments.psychographic: health-reset mindset; intimidated by 'serious runner' culture; buys online by default
segments.behavioral: buys shoes online; joins challenges; community-motivated

methods.recruitment: ~250 public Google/Yelp reviews of the actual Austin Fleet Feet store, keyword-coded
Fleet Feet site + Austin store pages, fit process, Happy Fit guarantee, vs DTC/Amazon
Peer-reviewed studies on shoe-fit injury + RunningUSA participation data + Strava year-in-sport
Intercept survey at group runs/events - runs as week-0 baseline inside the measurement plan

findings.finding: ~90% of new runners quit within a year; academic studies link wrong-fit shoes to injury-driven dropout - the fit problem is the category's retention killer
Austin-store reviews praise the gait analysis + Happy Fit guarantee specifically - the service is the thing locals actually rave about
Local reviews + event listings show a real run community exists but is invisible to non-customers - the asset is there, the awareness isn't
DTC wins on convenience and price; the store's only durable edge is relationship + fit - confirmed by industry and local data

assumptions.text: Gross margin ~45% on specialty running retail
$4,500 paid social at ~$7 CPM = ~640K impressions + ~60K organic community
8 event/community shifts at ~$300 each (group-run support, clinics, signage)
RUNCITY code: $20 off first fitted pair; netted in revenue
Repeat purchase ~40% within 12 months (runners replace shoes every 300-500 miles)

programs.name: Community Run Takeover
programs.mechanic: Sponsor + host weekly group runs at the Austin store: free pace groups, post-run fit clinic, 'first visit free' card + QR. Community first, sale second.

programs.name: Run Your City Challenge
programs.mechanic: Free 4-week challenge: run Austin landmarks, tag the store, finishers get fit consult + $20 off. City-as-campaign.

programs.name: Fit First Clinics
programs.mechanic: In-store gait-analysis clinics + 'why your shoes hurt' educational nights - the service IS the marketing [R2].

programs.name: Miles Club
programs.mechanic: Email/SMS runner-retention series: shoe-mileage reminders, local run calendars, member perks - replaces shoes at 400-mile marks [R4].

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: new runners buy online, get hurt in the wrong shoe, and quit - while Fleet Feet's best asset (free fit + community) is invisible to them [R1][R3].
Solution: Run Your City - community runs, a city-wide challenge, fit-first clinics, and a retention club that turns a store visit into a membership.
45-day goal: 150 purchases, 600 captures, +15 pts 'my running community' [O1-O3].
slides.notes: Sell the fit, not the shoe.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Running shoes + expert fitting: $120-180 shoes, free in-store gait analysis, 60-day Happy Fit guarantee [S1][R2].
The product isn't the shoe - it's the fit: a service no website can copy [R2][R4].
The Austin store already runs weekly group runs + clinics - a real community asset [R3][S2].
Austin's trail/run culture is a local moat no national ad can buy [S5].

slides.title: Company & Position
bullets: Running-specialty franchise with ~250 stores nationally + a real Austin location and run community [S1][S4][S2].
Competes against one-click DTC: the answer is relationship and fit, not price [R4].
Positioning gap: 'shoe store' is commoditized; 'your running community' is unclaimed locally.
Campaign claims the community.
slides.notes: Franchise retail - awareness is the gap.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1 (primary): 150 attributed purchases via RUNCITY + event QR at ~$140 AOV [O1].
O2: 600 email/SMS captures from runs, clinics, challenge [O2].
O3: 700K impressions; +15 pts 'my running community' on pre/post survey (n=150 + holdout) [O3].
Baseline: current list; week-0 survey; POS code report.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1: new + returning runners 18-40 - health-reset buyers who default to online; intimidated by 'serious runner' culture; Austin metro [S3][S5].
P2: established runners + gear loyalists 30-60 - repeat buyers, community-embedded [R4].
P1 is the growth the store needs; P2 is the revenue base.

slides.title: Research Methodology & Results
bullets: Local review analysis: ~250 Google/Yelp reviews of the actual Austin store, keyword-coded [R2][R3].
Academic + industry review: peer-reviewed shoe-fit injury studies + RunningUSA + Strava data [R1][S3].
Digital shelf audit: Fleet Feet site, Austin store, fit process, vs DTC/Amazon [S1][S2].
Measurement plan: pre/post intercept survey (n=150) at events as week-0 baseline [M1].

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: [R1] New runners quit from wrong shoes -> sell fit, not shoes: 'get fitted, stay running'.
[R2] Fit service is the moat -> clinics and gait analysis ARE the marketing events.
[R3] Community already exists -> amplify the run group, don't invent it.
[R4] DTC wins on convenience -> win on relationship: challenge + club, not discounts alone.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Theme: Run Your City - the store as the community's home base.
Push-pull: community runs create belonging (pull); challenge + clinics convert to fitted sales (push) [R3][A4].
Service as ad: the gait analysis IS the marketing moment [R2].
PESO: paid geo-social, earned local-run PR, shared challenge content, owned email/SMS + Miles Club.

slides.title: Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $13,950: paid social $4.5K [A4]; creators $2.4K [A6]; events $2.4K [A7]; production $550 [A10]; RUNCITY fund $3K [A8]; contingency ~9% [A11].
Funnel: 700K impressions x 2.8% CTR x 0.75% visit-to-purchase = ~150 purchases = $21K revenue [A1][A4].
GP 45% = $9.5K; direct ROI ~-27% - a community-proof budget; payback via 40% repeat at 400-mile replacement [A2][A13].
Conservative (50%): 75 purchases, ROI ~-64%; but the community asset persists past the spend [A15].

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: purchases via RUNCITY + QR UTMs; target 150; POS report; weekly [O1].
O2: captures; target 600; Klaviyo; weekly [O2].
O3: impressions 700K + perception +15 pts; pre/post survey w/ holdout [O3].
Trigger: <25 check-ins per event by week 3 -> shift spend to challenge + clinics.

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Fleet Feet owns the two things online can't copy: a free expert fit and a real running community - the local reviews prove it.
Run Your City sells belonging, not shoes - and the judges can literally join the Saturday run.
A local store, local data, local prop: the strongest district pitch there is.
